name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination
Heavy outside spending in the Democratic primary, not the general
model.rationale: The seat's D+32 lean makes the Democratic nominee a heavy favorite regardless of the primary upset, and Polymarket prices the Democratic side near 97%. The Republican nominee has shown little fundraising capacity, leaving no evidence of a competitive general election.
model.watch: A serious third-party or independent challenge, or unusually low turnout in a low-profile open seat, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Adriano Espaillat lost renomination, so this heavily Democratic Upper Manhattan seat will be defended by Darializa Avila Chevalier, who won a costly primary backed by substantial outside spending on both sides. The district's D+32 partisan lean makes the general election a formality in most cycles. Jomo Williams, the Republican nominee, has reported little or no fundraising and no outside support.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The main uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile open seat, not the likely winner.
